work.summary: Owned the 0-to-1 development of an AI product, building a LangGraph agent harness for hybrid RAG and tools, a secure multi-tenant FastAPI/PostgreSQL backend, and ingestion workers for Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack, and Teams. Improved answer relevance and tenant security with Milvus, Elasticsearch BM25, cross-encoder reranking, and ACL filters; deployed with Azure Container Apps, GitHub Actions, monitoring, and LangSmith.

Engineered a multi-agent long-form article generator using LangGraph, RAG, and STORM-based conversation simulations. Built planner, writer, and editor feedback loops plus a custom LLM-as-a-judge framework that achieved a 70% win rate over GPT-4o and a 5.04-point QA improvement.

Owned architecture, proofs of concept, deployment, and production support for 150+ priority enterprise workloads, resolving 400+ production issues. Built automation that reduced SLA misses by 70% and resolution time by 27%, alongside reusable Python ETL pipelines and developer tooling using Dataflow, Apache Beam, Composer, BigQuery, and Vertex AI.

Refactored NIOS by removing legacy implementations, unnecessary dependencies, and non-DNS functionality, reducing startup time by 25% while simplifying the codebase. Developed reusable network-service management components for the web UI using C++, React, and Angular.

publications.name: Reinforcement Learning for Improving Coherence of Multi-turn Responses in Deep Learning-Based Chatbots
publications.publisher: roceedings of International Conference on Communication, Circuits, and Systems
publications.summary: Chatbots are still far behind in their ability to hold meaningful conversations. The objective of the work is to implement and improve the multi-turn responses of deep learning-based chatbots. Multi-turn response is the ability of a chatbot to give coherent and sensible responses in successive turns. Firstly, sequence to sequence (Seq2Seq) model was built, and its responses were analyzed by varying training parameters. Secondly, the reinforcement learning (RL) method using the Seq2Seq model was implemented, and it is demonstrated that this improves coherence in multi-turn conversations. The RL model performed better than the Seq2Seq model in terms of BiLingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score with a score of 0.3334 compared to 0.2336 of the Seq2Seq model. Average conversation length was found to increase with RL with 3.75 turns compared to 3.05 turns with Seq2Seq.
